Rashi on Niddah 37a:10:1.hebrew: אלא - לא תוקי כדתרצה לטמויי במשא, אלא ודאי לסתירה. ובעיין לא תפשוט, דאנן לרבנן בעינן, ואת פשטת מדר"א:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:10:1.english: Rather - Do not establish [the baraita] as you answered, [that it is] to render [the drop] impure through carrying; rather, [it is] certainly for negating [the clean days]. And our dilemma you cannot resolve [from this], for we were asking according to the Rabbis, and you resolved [it] from Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:12:1.hebrew: ש"מ - מדנקט לשון גרמא, מכלל דקיימא ליה דבר הגורם סותר:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:12:1.english: Conclude from it - Since he used the language of causation, by implication he maintains that a thing that causes [impurity] negates [the count].

Rashi on Niddah 37a:13:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר היא - דאמר אונס סותר, ואינו גורם:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:13:1.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer - Who said [that an emission due to] circumstances beyond one's control negates [the clean days], and does not cause [zivah].

Rashi on Niddah 37a:14:1.hebrew: מהו שתעלה - אם ילדה בזוב ובימי לידתה לא ראתה, מהו שיעלה לה לנקיים, ולא תצטרך לספור אחריהן:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:14:1.english: What is [the law as to whether] it counts - If she gave birth during [a state of] zivah, and during the days of her childbirth she did not see [blood], what is [the law as to whether] it counts for her toward the clean [days], and [thus] she will not need to count after them?

Rashi on Niddah 37a:14:2.hebrew: אינה סותרת - אם היתה זבה ופסקה והתחילה לספור וילדה, אינה סותרת. וימי לידתה, אפי' אינה רואה בהן, אין משלימין לספירתה, אלא משלמת אחריהן אם טהרה:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:14:2.english: It does not negate - If she was a zava and [the bleeding] ceased, and she began to count, and gave birth, [the birth] does not negate [her count]. And the days of her childbirth [impurity], even if she does not see [blood] during them, do not complete her count; rather, she completes [her count] after them, if she is clean.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:17:1.english: From her zivah - [The verse states:] "And she shall count for herself" from her zivah.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:17:2.hebrew: ולא מנגעה - כיון שטהרה מזובה, סופרת מיד ותביא קרבן לזיבתה, ואז תטהר מלטמא בועלה, ואפילו מנוגעת, ולא צריכה להמתין עד שתטהר אף מנגעה:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:17:2.english: And not from her affliction - Once she is cleansed of her zivah, she counts immediately and brings an offering for her zivah, and then she is purified from defiling one who has intercourse with her, even if [she is] afflicted [with leprosy]; and she does not need to wait until she is purified also from her affliction.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:17:3.hebrew: ולא מלידתה - כיון שטהרה מזובה, סופרת מיד ואינה צריכה להמתין עד שיעברו ימי לידתה. אלמא, ילדה בימי ספירה — אינה סותרת ועולה:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:17:3.english: And not from her childbirth - Once she has become pure from her ziva, she counts immediately and does not need to wait until the days of her childbirth have passed. Evidently, [if] she gave birth during the days of counting, [the birth] does not negate [the count] and [the days] count [toward the clean days].

Rashi on Niddah 37a:1:1.english: Sheila went and said to his wife: "Prepare provisions for me" - [I.e.,] burial shrouds.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:1:2.english: Matters - So that he will not inform against me before Rav.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:1:3.hebrew: דקא פרח אסא - רגילין היו להניח הדס על המטה, וההדס של אלו פורח היה והולך ממטה למטה:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:1:3.english: That the myrtle was flying - They were accustomed to place myrtle on the bier, and the myrtle of these [sages] was flying and moving from bier to bier.

Rashi on Niddah 37a:2:1.english: Labor pains, what is [the law as to whether] she negates in zivah - [Does she negate] all that she counted?

Rashi on Niddah 37a:3:1.hebrew: דבר הגורם - לידי זיבה, אם ראתה שלש; והאי לאו גורם הוא, דלא אתיא בה לידי זיבה. ואי קשיא: והרי קרי, שאינו גורם כדקי"ל, וסותר? ההיא לאו סתירה היא, דחד יומא הוא דסותר; וכי קא בעי רבא — לסתור הכל:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:3:1.english: Something that causes - [To enter] into [a state of] zivah, if she were to see [it] three [times]; and this [blood of labor pains] is not a cause [of zivah], as she does not enter into a state of zivah through it. And if you should object: But behold, [an emission of] semen (keri), which does not cause [one to become a zav], as we maintain, and yet it negates [the clean days]? That is not [a full] negation, because it negates only one day; whereas when Rava raised his dilemma, [it was whether it] negates the entire [count].

Rashi on Niddah 37a:4:1.hebrew: שאינו גורם - כדקי"ל, ולא מחמת אונסו:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:4:1.english: That it does not cause - As is established for us: "And not due to circumstances beyond his control."

Rashi on Niddah 37a:4:2.hebrew: וסותר - כדאמר בפירקין, ברביעית אין בודקין אותו:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:4:2.english: And it negates - As [the Gemara] says in our chapter: "Regarding the fourth [sighting], one does not examine him."

Rashi on Niddah 37a:5:1.hebrew: לאיי - באמת, אונס נמי גורם הוא לידי זוב, שאם ראה שתים שלא באונס ושלישית באונס, מצטרפין לקרבן, דתנן: שלישית אין בודקין אותו:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:5:1.english: Indeed - In truth, [an emission due to] circumstances beyond one's control also causes [one to enter the state of] zivah, for if he experienced two [sightings] not due to circumstances beyond his control and a third due to circumstances beyond his control, they combine for [the obligation to bring] a sacrifice, as we learned [in a mishna]: "[After] the third [sighting], one does not examine him."

Rashi on Niddah 37a:9:1.hebrew: לקרבן אמרתי - דבעי בדיקה, ולא לסתירה:
Rashi on Niddah 37a:9:1.english: I said [this] for an offering - That it requires examination, and not for negating [the clean days].

Tosafot on Niddah 37a:13:1.hebrew: נקטינן דאין קושי סותר - מכאן משמע דלא דרשי אתים, אם לא שנפרש לעיל (נדה דף לה.) ורבנן אתים לא דרשי היינו להך דרשא; אך משמע דלא דרשי כלל:
Tosafot on Niddah 37a:13:1.english: We have a tradition that [labor] pain does not negate - From here it is implied that [the Rabbis] do not expound instances of the word "et" (etim), unless we explain that earlier (Niddah 35a), "and the Rabbis do not expound etim" refers [only] to that [specific] exposition; yet it implies that they do not expound [them] at all.

Tosafot on Niddah 37a:14:1.hebrew: אביי אמר אינה סותרת ואינה עולה - כתב רש"י בתשובה אחת, דאביי מודה דימי לידה שאינה רואה בהן עולים לספירת זיבתה, דהכי מוכח פרק בא סימן (לקמן נדה דף נד:) מן הברייתא, והכא אליבא דר' מרינוס קיימין. תדע, דאין רגילות למיבעי חדא מילתא בתרי דוכתי, דבעי לה הכא ובשילהי בפ' בא סימן (שם). ותו, היאך חולק אביי אברייתא דהתם? ותו, דמה להם לאביי ורבא להזכיר סתירה? לא היה להם להזכיר אלא עלייה, דפליגי בה! אלא, אליבא דר' מרינוס בעי: מהו שתעלה? דמדנקט "אין לידה סותרת", ולא קאמר נמי "דעולה", מכלל דסבירא ליה דאינה עולה; או דלמא הא בהא תליא, כיון דאינה סותרת ע"כ עולה, מ"ואחר תטהר" – שלא תהא טומאה מפסקת ביניהן. ומייתי רבא: מנא אמינא לה? דמסתמא רבי מרינוס לא פליג אקרא. ואביי מייתי: מנא אמינא לה? דאיכא תנא דפליג אברייתא דבא סימן (שם), ואיכא למימר דר' מרינוס סבירא ליה נמי הכי, מדלא קאמר ר' מרינוס "אינה סותרת ועולה". וה"ה דהוה מצי אביי לאתויי ברייתא דטועה בהמפלת (לעיל נדה דף כח:) דסברה דאין עולה; אלא דרבא הוה מוקי לה כר' אליעזר, כדמוקי ברייתא דבסמוך. כן פרש"י. ומה שפירש דמייתי רבא מנא אמינא לה דמסתמא לא פליג ר' מרינוס אקרא – קשה, דהא ע"כ ר"א פליג! וי"ל, דהוה מצי למימר: וליטעמיך, אלא בלאו הכי דחי ליה אביי שפיר. ומה שפירש ברייתא דהמפלת (שם דף כח:) מוקי לה רבא כרבי אליעזר – דוקא בהא הויא כרבי אליעזר, דאין עולין לה; אבל לגמרי לא הויא כר' אליעזר, דהא מוקי לה כר"ע דבעי ספורים בפנינו, ור"א פליג עליה בפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף ז:). ור"ת מפרש, דהלכתא כאביי דאין עולין, וכברייתא דהמפלת (שם דף כט:). ומדקדק מדלא קאמר עלה (לעיל נדה ל.): ש"מ ארבע, דימי לידה אין עולין – לאפוקי מן הברייתא דלעיל ללוי לחד שינוייא, ומברייתא דבא סימן (לקמן נדה דף נד:) דסברי דעולין; אלא אינו מונה אלא דברים של חדוש, אבל הא פשיטא לן דאין עולין. ועוד אומר ר"ת, דברייתא דבא סימן איכא למימר כדמפרש ליה רב פפא, משום דאימא ילדה זכר, להכי עולה שבוע שני לספירת זיבתה. ודבריו נראה טפי, מדקתני: "ואין קרבנו נאכל"; א"כ איכא למימר: אימר לא ילדה, ואפי' ילדה – אימא ילדה זכר. ותדע דלא קיבל דברי רב הונא דהתם ולא הדר ביה, אלא סבר דאין עולין, מדקאמר בשמעתין: "רב פפא אמר ע"כ הקישן הכתוב"; ואי סבר עולין, א"כ ע"כ צריך לאוקמי כר"א כדמוקי רבא, ואמאי דחיק לאוקמי כרבנן דר"א דאמרי אין דנין אפשר משאי אפשר, כיון דבלאו הכי צריך לאוקמי כר"א דאמר אין עולין? אלא ודאי לא הדר ביה. ומיהו, אי גרסינן לעיל: דאמר סותר רבי אלעזר, והכא רבי אליעזר – אין להוכיח כלום. ודברי רב פפא דלקמן איכא למימר דאינו עיקר; אע"פ דהוי ספק ספיקא, שבוע שני אינו עולה לספירת זיבתה, דאיכא למיחש דילמא נקבה היא, כדאמר רב הונא התם, משום דאיכא נמי ספק ספיקא בסוף ימי טוהר דסתרה לה, כדפרישית לעיל גבי המפלת חיה ועוף (דף כז. סד"ה חומר). ומיהו, כיון דאין קרבנה נאכל, איכא בלאו הכי ספק ספיקא: שמא לא ראתה, ואפילו ראתה שמא לא ילדה. ואומר ר"ת, דימי לידה שאינה רואה בהן הוא למ"ד מיע"ל קג"ם, ולא לחי העומד מאיליו בפ"ק דעירובין (דף טו.). ורב סעדיה כתב, דנשים שלנו דחשבינן להו כיולדות בזוב, אם עברו ימי טומאת ז' לזכר או י"ד לנקבה, וספרה שבעה נקיים בימי טוהר או אפילו בימי טומאה, מותרת לבעלה עד מ' לזכר ופ' לנקבה, אע"פ שרואה דם – הכתוב קראו דם טוהר, שכן שנו חכמים: ימי לידה שאינה רואה בהן עולים לה לימי ספירת זיבתה. הרי בהדיא חולק על ר"ת! והא דלא קאמר בהמפלת (שם דף ל.) "ש"מ ד'", איכא למימר: משום דלא קאמר אלא היכא דמצי למימר "הא מני פלוני היא", כדקאמר: ש"מ ר"ע היא, ש"מ ר"ש היא, ש"מ טבילה בזמנה מצוה לאפוקי מדר' יוסי בר' יהודה; אבל בהא דאין עולין לא מצי למימר "הא מני רבי אליעזר היא", דלאביי לכ"ע אין עולין:
Tosafot on Niddah 37a:14:1.english: Abaye said: It does not negate and does not count - Rashi wrote in a responsum that Abaye concedes that days of childbirth on which she does not see [blood] count toward the counting of her zivah, for so it is proven in the chapter Ba Siman (below, Niddah 54b) from the baraita; and here [in our sugya], we stand according to [the opinion of] Rabbi Marinus. Know [that this is so], for it is not usual to raise a dilemma about one matter in two places, as it is asked here and [also] at the end of the chapter Ba Siman (ibid.). And furthermore, how could Abaye dispute the baraita there? And furthermore, why did Abaye and Rava need to mention negation (setirah)? They should have mentioned only counting (aliyyah), over which they disagree! Rather, according to [the opinion of] Rabbi Marinus [the Gemara] asks: What is [the ruling according to him as to] whether it counts? For since he formulated [his ruling as]: "Childbirth does not negate," and did not also state "and it counts," does it follow that he holds that it does not count? Or perhaps this is dependent on that: since it does not negate, perforce it counts, from [the verse], "and after that she shall be pure" (Leviticus 15:28)—[which implies] that an impurity should not intervene between them? And Rava brings [support, asking]: "From where do I say it?": for presumably Rabbi Marinus does not dispute the verse. And Abaye brings [support, asking]: "From where do I say it?": that there is a tanna who disputes the baraita of Ba Siman (ibid.), and it can be said that Rabbi Marinus also holds thus, since Rabbi Marinus did not say "it does not negate and it counts." And likewise, Abaye could have brought the baraita of the confused woman (to'ah) in [the chapter] HaMappelet (above, Niddah 28b [29b]), which holds that it does not count; but [Abaye did not cite it because] Rava would have established it in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, just as he establishes the nearby baraita [on 37b]. Thus explained Rashi. And as for what [Rashi] explained, that Rava brings "From where do I say it?" because presumably Rabbi Marinus does not dispute the verse—this is difficult, for perforce Rabbi Eliezer disputes [it]! And one can say that [Abaye] could have said [to Rava]: "And according to your reasoning [does not Rabbi Eliezer dispute it]?" But even without this, Abaye rebuffed him well. And as for what [Rashi] explained, that Rava would establish the baraita of HaMappelet (ibid. 28b) in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer—it is specifically in this [matter alone] that it is like Rabbi Eliezer, [namely] that they do not count for her; but completely it is not like Rabbi Eliezer, for [the Gemara on 30a] establishes it like Rabbi Akiva, who requires [the clean days to be] counted in our presence (sefurim befanenu), and Rabbi Eliezer disputes him in the first chapter (above, Niddah 7b). And Rabbeinu Tam explains that the halakha is in accordance with Abaye, that they do not count, and in accordance with the baraita of HaMappelet (ibid. 29b). And he infers [this] from the fact that [the Gemara] did not state regarding it (above, Niddah 30a): "Conclude from it four [rulings]: that days of childbirth do not count"—to exclude the baraita above according to Levi under one resolution [29a], and [to exclude] the baraita of Ba Siman (below, Niddah 54b), which hold that they do count! Rather, it enumerates only novel points, but this [ruling] is obvious to us, that they do not count. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam says that the baraita of Ba Siman can be explained as Rav Pappa explained it: because one can say [perhaps] she gave birth to a male, therefore the second week counts toward the counting of her zivah. And his words [Rav Pappa's explanation] appear more [reasonable], since it teaches: "and its offering is not eaten"; if so, one can say: say [perhaps] she did not give birth [at all], and even if she did give birth, say she gave birth to a male. And know that he [Rav Pappa] did not accept the words of Rav Huna there [on 54b] and did not retract, but rather held that they do not count, from [the fact] that in our sugya, Rav Pappa said: "Perforce the verse juxtaposed them" [to explain the baraita according to the Rabbis who dispute Rabbi Eliezer]; and if he held that they count, if so, perforce he would need to establish it in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer as Rava establishes it! And why would he exert himself to establish it in accordance with the Rabbis of Rabbi Eliezer who say "one does not derive the possible from the impossible," when regardless he must establish it in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer who said they do not count? Rather, certainly he did not retract. However, if our reading above [37a:13] is: "the one who said [labor pains] negate is Rabbi Eleazar," whereas here [37b:7] it is "Rabbi Eliezer," nothing can be proven. And the words of Rav Pappa below [54b]—one can say that it is not primary: even though it is a double doubt (safek sefeika), the second week does not count toward the counting of her zivah, for one must be concerned that perhaps it was a female as Rav Huna said there, because there is also a double doubt at the end of the days of purity that it negates for her, as I explained above regarding "one who miscarries a beast or bird" (page 27a, end of dibbur hamatchil Chomer). However, since its offering is not eaten, there is regardless a double doubt: perhaps she did not see [blood], and even if she saw [blood], perhaps she did not give birth. And Rabbeinu Tam says that [the case of] days of childbirth on which she does not see [blood] is the [letter] Lamed of YA"L K-G"M [i.e., leida, where the halakha follows Abaye], and not [the Lamed of] a side post that stands on its own (leḥi ha'omed me'elav) in the first chapter of Eruvin (15a). And Rav Saadia wrote that our women, whom we consider as women who give birth as a zava: if the days of impurity passed—seven for a male or fourteen for a female—and she counted seven clean days during the days of purity or even during the days of impurity, she is permitted to her husband until forty [days] for a male and eighty for a female; even though she sees blood, the verse designated it "blood of purity," for so the Sages taught: "Days of childbirth on which she does not see [blood] count for her toward the days of counting her zivah." Behold, he explicitly disputes Rabbeinu Tam! And that which [the Gemara] did not state in [the chapter] HaMappelet (ibid. 30a), "Conclude from it four [rulings]": one can say [it is] because it only states [conclusions] where it can say "In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is so-and-so," as it says: "Conclude from it that it is Rabbi Akiva," "Conclude from it that it is Rabbi Shimon," "Conclude from it that immersion at its proper time is a mitzvah, to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehudah"; but regarding this [ruling], that they do not count, it could not say "In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer," because according to Abaye, according to everyone they do not count.

Tosafot on Niddah 37a:14:2.hebrew: רבא אמר אינה סותרת - וא"ת: והא רב סובר בפ"ב (דף טו) דאי אפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם, וא"כ תסתור, דהכא בעינן שבעה נקיים מדם? וי"ל, דרב אליבא דר' מרינוס קאמר, כדפרישית, וסבר דאפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם, דהא קאמר דאינה סותרת:
Tosafot on Niddah 37a:14:2.english: Rava said: [The birth] does not negate - And if you say: But doesn't Rav [i.e., Rava] hold in the second chapter (15) that the opening of the womb is impossible without blood, and if so, [the birth] should negate [her count], for here we require seven [days] clean from blood? And one can answer: Rav [i.e., Rava] was speaking according to Rabbi Marinus, as I explained; and [Rabbi Marinus] holds that the opening of the womb is possible without blood, for behold, he says that [the birth] does not negate [the count].

Tosafot on Niddah 37a:3:1.hebrew: דבר הגורם סותר כו' - וא"ת: יולדת בזוב תוכיח, דסותרת לרב דאמר מעין אחד הוא, אע"ג דדם טוהר אינו גורם שום טומאה? וי"ל, דדם טוהר חשיב גורם טפי, כיון שאם לא ילדה, הויא זבה או נדה לרב דאמר מעין אחד הוא; ולא דמי לקושי, דלעולם דם שתראה מחמת קושי לידה אינו גורם זיבה:
Tosafot on Niddah 37a:3:1.english: A substance that causes [zivah] negates, etc. - And if you say: Let [the case of] a woman who gives birth as a zavah (yoledet be-zov) prove [otherwise], for she negates [her clean days] according to Rav, who said [that pure and impure blood emanate from] one source, even though blood of purity (dam tohar) does not cause any impurity? And one can say [in response]: Blood of purity is considered more of a cause, since had she not given birth, she would have become a zavah or a niddah according to Rav, who said [that pure and impure blood emanate from] one source; and it is not comparable to [blood of] labor pains (koshi), for blood that she sees on account of labor pains can never cause zivah.
